subject: High 429s / latency after quota window reset — investigation and exec attention
messages:
From: Ken Huang <ken.huang@brightline.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Brightline SRE <sre@brightline.com>, procurement@brightline.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 01:12:00 -0700
Subject: High error rate and 429s since 09:40 PT — urgent

Hi Sean / Monica,

We started seeing a sharp uptick in 429s and elevated p95 latency across our integration around 09:40 PT this morning. Traffic pattern hasn't changed from our side — same payloads, same concurrency. Key symptoms:
- ~25% 429s on generation endpoints for ~35 minutes
- p95 latency jumped from 210ms -> 1.2s
- Some inference requests returning 5xx as the system retries

Attached is a short sample of the first 200 errors (error-sample-20250630.log). This is impacting our production checkout flow; we are triaging on our side but need Redwood to investigate rate/quota/burst configuration immediately.

Can you confirm whether any quota window/auto-replenish changes rolled out in us-west-2 this morning? If there's a capacity or rate-limiter regression, we need a temporary mitigation (increase credits, route to another pool, or fallback to an earlier model) while you fix the root cause.

Thanks — Ken
Ken Huang
Head of Platform, Brightline Health
ken.huang@brightline.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Ken Huang <ken.huang@brightline.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High error rate and 429s since 09:40 PT — urgent

Ken — thanks for the flag and the log sample. We acknowledge the impact and I’m escalating to Eng + CS immediately.

Immediate actions we are taking (in parallel):
1) Monica to open a support incident and propose a manual temporary credit/top-up to avoid immediate user impact.
2) Karthik/Dylan to triage the rate-limiter and replenish window config in us-west-2; we’ll surface a hotfix if we confirm a misconfiguration.
3) I am looping Marissa for exec visibility in case Brightline requests an SLA credit or additional remediation.

We’ll update you within 30 minutes with a short mitigation plan.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ken Huang <ken.huang@brightline.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High error rate and 429s since 09:40 PT — urgent

Ken — I opened support case #32719 and uploaded your log sample. We can do a one-time manual credit top-up for the Brightline prod org while Eng investigates — would that remove pressure on your short-term traffic?

Proposed quick mitigations (if acceptable to Brightline):
- Manual +25% burst credit for 1 hour (immediate)
- Route a subset of traffic to a reserved capacity pool in us-east-1 (if you can accept slight latency increase)
- Temporary model fallback to a smaller quantized variant for non-critical calls (we can toggle at your API key level)

Please confirm which mitigations you want us to apply now. We’ll keep the manual credit visible in the support ticket and follow up with a Mutual Action Plan (attached once we align).

—Monica
Monica Patel
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Ken Huang <ken.huang@brightline.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High error rate and 429s since 09:40 PT — urgent

Folks — initial triage notes:
- We identified a config change in the auto-replenish service deployed at 08:58 PT to us-west-2. The new release unintentionally set the replenish_window_ms to 0 for a subset of customers with dedicated burst profiles. With window=0, client credit counters were not being replenished at window boundaries, which explains the rapid credit exhaustion and ensuing 429s.
- Logs show credit deduction still happening correctly; replenish cron jobs executed but the window parameter short-circuited.

Immediate remediation plan (ETA minutes-hours):
A) Emergency rollback of the 08:58 release to the prior configuration (target ETA 20–30 minutes). This will restore the replenish_window_ms to the expected 60_000ms value.
B) As a soft mitigation, we can issue a manual credit top-up to Brightline to buy time (Monica to coordinate).
C) Post-rollback, we’ll run a targeted smoke test on Brightline org keys and monitor 429/latency for 60 minutes.
D) Follow-up hotfix to add safety checks preventing zero-window values and a canary check in the deploy pipeline (ETA 2 business days).

I’ll own the rollback and verification. I’m attaching (inline) a short excerpt from the replenish service logs showing the parameter set to 0:

---- log excerpt ----
[2025-06-30T08:58:13Z] deploy: auto-replenish v2.7.8 -> config applied to us-west-2
[2025-06-30T08:58:13Z] config: burst_profile=standard, replenish_window_ms=0
[2025-06-30T09:02:05Z] credit-manager: deduct org=brightline credits=-
[2025-06-30T09:02:05Z] rate-limiter: 429 returned to client key=org:brightline
---- end ----

Will update with rollback completion timestamp.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ken Huang <ken.huang@brightline.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High error rate and 429s since 09:40 PT — urgent

Team — thanks for the fast escalation. Sean/Monica: please handle Brightline’s immediate business impact first (manual credit + routing), and confirm whether Brightline requires an SLA credit or contract remediation. If so, escalate to Finance/SalesOps (I’ll assist).

Karthik — prioritize the rollback and the hotfix safe-guards. After rollback and verification, prepare a concise postmortem with customer-facing summary and timeline (we’ll need this for Brightline and Sales leadership).

Ken — on behalf of Redwood, I’m sorry for the disruption. We will:
- Apply a manual top-up (Monica has the details)
- Roll back the deploy and validate within the hour
- Provide a one-page summary and proposed credit (if SLA impacted) within 24 hours

Please keep me posted on whether Brightline wants a call with Execs; if so, we’ll schedule for today.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Ken Huang <ken.huang@brightline.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 17:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High error rate and 429s since 09:40 PT — urgent

Ken — quick summary and next steps now that we’ve stabilized: 

What happened:
- A deploy to the auto-replenish service introduced a replenish_window_ms=0 for certain burst profiles in us-west-2, causing credits to not replenish at window boundaries and triggering widespread 429s for Brightline traffic between ~09:00–09:40 PT.

Immediate remediation applied (completed by 10:15 PT):
- Rolled back the 08:58 deploy and restored replenish_window_ms to 60000ms.
- Issued a manual +30% burst credit to Brightline for 2 hours to remove residual pressure.
- Routed a small % of Brightline traffic to a reserved pool in us-east-1 during verification.

Next actions (timeline):
1) Engineering hotfix: validation to prevent zero-value windows in config and a canary gate (ETA 2 business days) — owner: Karthik.
2) Postmortem and customer-facing summary (ETA 24 hours) — owner: Sean / Monica.
3) SLA review and credit proposal: Marissa will coordinate and revert within 24 hours.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan-brightline.pdf

We appreciate Brightline’s patience — we’ll follow up in the support ticket with monitoring dashboards and the postmortem. If you’d like an exec call to discuss credits and contract impacts, I can arrange that this afternoon.

Best — Sean

Attachments: mutual-action-plan-brightline.pdf
